question: A 33-year-old woman comes to the physician because of a 3-day history of dry cough and low-grade fever. Four months ago, she was diagnosed with major depressive disorder and started treatment with fluoxetine. Physical examination shows no abnormalities. A diagnosis of upper respiratory infection is made and a medication is prescribed to relieve her symptoms. A drug with which of the following mechanisms of action should be avoided in this patient?
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "Fluoxetine" -> "increased serotonin levels" -> "risk of serotonin syndrome" -> "avoid NMDA receptor inhibition" -> 85%
CHAIN: "Fluoxetine" -> "increased serotonin levels" -> "risk of serotonin syndrome" -> "avoid H1 receptor inhibition" -> 70%
CHAIN: "Fluoxetine" -> "increased serotonin levels" -> "risk of serotonin syndrome" -> "avoid α-adrenergic receptor stimulation" -> 60%
CHAIN: "Fluoxetine" -> "increased serotonin levels" -> "risk of serotonin syndrome" -> "avoid mucoid disulfide bond disruption" -> 50%
CHAIN: "Fluoxetine" -> "increased serotonin levels" -> "risk of serotonin syndrome" -> "avoid reduction in secretion viscosity" -> 50%
analysis: The patient is on fluoxetine, a selective serotonin reuptake inhibitor (SSRI), which can increase serotonin levels. Medications that inhibit NMDA glutamate receptors, such as dextromethorphan, can also increase serotonin levels and potentially lead to serotonin syndrome when combined with SSRIs. Therefore, a drug with this mechanism of action should be avoided.
